Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned: us-east-3 staged driver rotation + rolling restarts (targeted windows)

Hi Ian / Acme platform team —

Heads-up: Redwood will perform a staged rotation of NIC/kernel drivers and rolling node restarts in the us-east-3 region next week. This maintenance is to deploy a compatibility fix for the new CUDA driver set and an updated NIC firmware that reduces packet drops under bursty traffic.

What to expect:
- Target windows (UTC): July 14 02:00–06:00 and July 14 22:00–02:00 (we will split work across two windows to minimize blast radius).
- Impact: individual nodes will be restarted one at a time; most customer workloads will continue to serve through remaining capacity. Each node restart typically takes 3–7 minutes.
- Scope: dedicated and shared tenancy clusters in us-east-3 only (no config changes to Dedicated reserved pools outside us-east-3).
- Safety: automatic traffic draining, KV cache preservation, and immediate fallback to compatible model variant if an instance fails health checks.

Attachments: maintenance_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook), staged_schedule.csv (per-pool timing). Please review the runbook and let us know if you have any questions or request adjustments to the windows. We'll keep a public-facing status update on the maintenance page and send a short post-maintenance summary.

On-call contacts during the window:
- Jordan Blake — engineering lead (on-call): +1 415 555 0112
- Naomi Feldman — ops coordinator: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com

If you have any critical jobs that cannot tolerate a single-node rollover during that date range, flag them here and we'll evaluate an exclusion or alternative scheduling.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-maintenance: us-east-3 driver rotation — summary & next steps

Ian / Acme team —

Summary from today's work (completed within the adjusted windows):
- Status: Completed — all targeted clusters in us-east-3 were updated and restarted in a staged fashion.
- Impact: Several short per-node restarts occurred; we observed one node that failed the post-restart health check and was auto-rolled back to the previous variant. No customer-facing availability incidents were reported.
- Observed benefit: NIC error counters decreased by ~72% on updated machines over a 2-hour sample.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- We opened JIRA-OPS-2345 to capture the node that hit the rollback (postmortem and corrective driver build cadence).
- Postmortem timeline: we'll circulate an internal timeline and a short external summary by EOD Wednesday (2026-07-15).
- If you want the full runbook and evidence package (logs, kernel module hashes, firmware checksums), reply and we'll push the package to the shared drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcRunbookExample

Thanks for coordinating on the window changes and for providing the network diagram — it helped avoid the overlap with your batch job. Naomi will follow up with the postmortem email and the artifacts.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
